sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft caching guidance describes frequently reused copies, latency/source-load benefits, source authority and application fills; cache-aside documentation warns of overhead when hit rates are low.
Microsoft cache-aside lists application cache lookup, source fetch on miss, cache insertion then return, and explicitly disclaims consistency with source updates.
Microsoft guidance and cache-aside example assign reads/fills to the application and require a key for method parameters; private-data guidance supports separating answer-changing user inputs.

Microsoft cache-aside disclaims consistency and discusses staleness after writes. Its independently fetched source and later cache insertion allow the lesson's explicitly ordered old-fill race; delete cannot alter an already fetched value. Direct authoritative reads avoid this cache response.

Redis documents memory-limit eviction, LRU and noeviction errors; TTL-associated keys may be selected for eviction. AWS linked lesson source separately describes per-object lifetime versus capacity removal; neither operation refreshes source data.

AWS describes in-process caches diverging across servers and cold starts, and separate shared fleets reducing copies while adding operational and availability costs. This supports one-local versus common shared-access failure consequences.

AWS body describes simultaneous uncached requests and one pending request via coalescing; its recommendations explicitly include capping dependent-service requests, shedding load, and cache-disabled load tests.
